reasoning: Broad system-architecture paper (edge AI + IoT + blockchain + digital twin) in which the only segmentation content is a self-reported Mask R-CNN weed-segmentation IoU (94.2%) claim buried among disease/yield/pest subsystems; no primary UAV segmentation experiment or benchmark with retrievable, verifiable quantitative results is presented.

Evaluates CNN and Transformer architectures (U-Net, SegNet, DeepLabV3+, SegFormer, Swin-UNet, Mask2Former) for semantic segmentation of UAV-acquired RGB orthomosaics of Opuntia spp. and Agave crops, reporting IoU, Dice, BF, HD95 and per-image computational cost under a reproducible protocol (best Mask2Former IoU ~0.897).

Full text shows this is generic aerial semantic segmentation on the MBRSC Dubai Aerial Imagery Dataset (urban scenes) using weighted ensembles of ResNet34/InceptionV3/VGG16 U-Net backbones (87.06% Dice, 78.13% IoU); it is an urban remote-sensing benchmark with no crop/weed agricultural content.

YOLOv26 instance segmentation of Potato Virus Y (PVY) symptom regions in UAV RGB potato imagery (mAP@50 ~65%, precision 73%, recall 65%); although UAV-borne and mask-based, the segmented objects are disease symptoms, which falls under EXC-03 disease-classification.

U-Net/DeepLabv3 semantic segmentation of weeds in barley and rapeseed from UAV multispectral imagery with quantitative weed F1 (0.5833 best, 0.6274 after few-shot rapeseed transfer) and mIoU, including cross-field and cross-crop spatial generalization analysis.

VL-WS (CLIP embeddings + FiLM) performs fine-grained crop-weed pixel segmentation on a corpus including high-altitude UAV imagery, achieving mean Dice 91.64% and out-performing the CNN baseline by 4.98% across four benchmark datasets.

PRC-Net is a lightweight context-aware network for pixel-level soil/crop/weed segmentation of UAV multispectral imagery (WeedMap/Sesame, mIoU ~0.8397/0.6520/0.6961) explicitly designed for deployment under constrained edge-computing resources.

AgriJetsonBench is a reproducible deployment benchmark running crop/weed detection and segmentation models (incl. SegFormer-B0) on Jetson AGX Orin / Orin Nano, reporting on-device FPS, p95 latency and J/inference (e.g. SegFormer-B0 FP16 103.61 FPS, 9.44 ms); directly supplies RQ2 edge metrics for agricultural segmentation.

U-Net pixel-based weed/crop classification on UAV multispectral maize imagery comparing a low-cost sensor against MicaSense Altum, reporting weed-class F1 82% (Altum) / 76% (low-cost) with precision and recall.

WeedFormer (SegFormer-B2 + CBAM + ASPP) performs crop-weed semantic segmentation on UAV WeedsGalore imagery, achieving 80.27% mIoU and 98.81% pixel accuracy and outperforming DeepLabv3+ and SegFormer baselines.

UNet-ResNet semantic segmentation of background/crop (sorghum)/weed in UAV imagery with an integrated NAFNet deblurring module, reporting best mean Dice 0.9198 and a +27.7% relative Dice improvement on motion-blurred test data.

SCG-UNet performs semantic segmentation of weeds in soybean fields from fused UAV RGB+multispectral imagery, achieving mIoU 83.43%, Dice 79.50% and F1 80.77% with stable five-fold spatial block cross-validation.

Herbsat is a satellite-dominant multi-stage framework (segment-then-classify with hybrid U-Net/Mask R-CNN plus LSTM-CNN and DenseNet) for detecting and classifying Ayurvedic crop types in hill-region remote sensing; the imagery is primarily satellite and the task is crop-type identification/health management, not UAV crop-weed segmentation.

Implements YOLOv8 bounding-box detection of humans/friends/enemies (mAP 90.3) on a Jetson AGX Orin UAV for aerial surveillance; this is non-agricultural military/human detection, and it is box-based detection with no pixel segmentation masks.

YOLOv8n/l bounding-box detection of individual trees (manually labeled boxes) for forest vegetation-density monitoring from drone imagery (F1 up to 0.973); a forestry task with box-only detection and no crop/weed segmentation masks.

CamelinaWeed is a Data in Brief data-descriptor article publishing an annotated UAV RGB/multispectral weed dataset for Camelina sativa; it contains no trained models and no quantitative segmentation benchmark results (mIoU/Dice/F1) in full text, failing EXC-06 despite matching the agricultural domain.

Uses EfficientNet feature extraction with Random Forest + SVM classification to detect corn-earworm infestations in whole UAV multispectral/thermal images (90% classification accuracy); this is whole-image pest classification with no pixel-level segmentation masks.

Five U-Net variants (U-Net, Res-U-Net, Double U-Net, Modified U-Net, AU-Net) perform multi-class semantic segmentation of weeds and potato crop in drone RGB imagery (best Residual U-Net mean IoU 0.8021), assessed with Dice, IoU and Dice-loss metrics.

WF-UNet++ jointly maps maize water-stress levels and rust disease into a five-class space (soil/healthy vegetation/mild stress/high stress/rust) on UAV multispectral orthomosaics (mIoU 0.8623); the pixel classes are disease/stress states, i.e., crop disease-classification, not crop-weed segmentation (EXC-03).

Self-supervised MoCo-v3/MAE pretraining of Swin transformer encoders is evaluated on the downstream task of crop-weed semantic segmentation on UAV WeedMap multispectral data (5-100% training-data regimes, cross-sensor and cross-region generalization), reporting quantitative segmentation results against baselines.

VISA, a two-stream radiance/index segmentation network, performs pixel-level barley crop-weed segmentation on the four-year BAWSeg UAV multispectral benchmark, reporting mIoU 75.6% and weed-class IoU 63.5%.

Segments Kenaf (crop) seedlings from saline-alkali soil in UAV RGB imagery using FCN, U-Net, DeepLabV3+ and an SE-enhanced U-Net (IoU 85.99%, Dice 92.44%) for canopy-coverage estimation; UAV deep-learning crop pixel-level segmentation with quantitative metrics, though without a weed class.

Semantic-SAM fusion maps parcel-level crop fields by crop type from UAV RGB imagery (best mIoU 87.09%); the segmentation targets are field parcels and boundaries for parcel-level crop-type identification, not plant-level crop/weed segmentation, so it does not satisfy INC-01's crop/weed segmentation requirement.

ML-LodgingNet segments wheat-lodging (flattened vs standing) regions from UAV RGB+DSM data (IoU 89.42%/70.65%, 19.3 FPS on edge devices); although it reports on-device FPS, its masks map crop-condition/lodging status rather than crop/weed classes, failing INC-01 (EXC-03).

DPT/SegFormer/U-Net models perform pixel segmentation of sunflower inflorescences on a UAV RGB orthomosaic (DPT F-score 0.946, IoU 0.897) whose outputs feed inflorescence abundance/size indicators and a weighted head area index; the target is flower/inflorescence detection and counting, the flower/gray-zone domain excluded under EXC-03.

Link-adaptive edge-cloud inference (SegFormer-B3 student-teacher) segments plastic-mulch residue on sub-centimetre UAV field imagery (IoU 0.826, 72 ms median latency); despite strong edge-inference reporting, the segmented object is agricultural waste film, not crop or weed vegetation (EXC-03).
